depicted_event_note: The capture is almost certainly a later capture of period software on a period OS (likely in an emulator or VM). It is not a 1990s screenshot, and no capture date is known.
depicted_content: The front window is titled "FreeCell Game #14601". Its menu reads Game / Options / Help, with "Cards Left: 52" at the right. Below are four empty free cells, the FreeCell king icon and four empty home cells on green felt, with the columns dealt. Behind it is a "Tut's Tomb" window (Game / Help menu, "Time: 28"). A minimized File Manager icon sits on a grey Windows 3.x desktop, and a mouse pointer is visible.

identity_evidence.text: Title bar "FreeCell Game #14601"; menu "Game Options Help"; "Cards Left: 52"; the FreeCell king icon between free cells and home cells.

Windows 3.x chrome: a system-menu box at the left of each title bar and minimize/maximize arrow buttons at the right, with no close button. The active title bar is dithered, which fits a 16-colour display, and the file has a 13-colour palette. Not Windows 95 (no × close button, no 95 caption style) and not the Vista+ remake (no Aero chrome, no redesigned cards or menus).
Tut's Tomb, another game listed on Entertainment Pack 2 (WinWorld product page), is open behind FreeCell. A minimized File Manager icon is on the desktop.

WinWorld places the image in the gallery "Screenshots for Microsoft Entertainment Pack 2" with the caption "Microsoft Entertainment Pack 2 - Cards". The product page says the release contains Freecell, JigSawed, Pipe Dream, RattlerRace, Rodent's Revenge, Stones and Tut's Tomb, and that "This version is for Windows 3.0 and later."

The pixels cannot separate Windows 3.0 from 3.1, and cannot distinguish the Entertainment Pack 2 FreeCell binary from the Best of Microsoft Entertainment Pack or Win32s FreeCell running on Windows 3.1. The version is recorded as Windows 3.x-era Microsoft FreeCell; the Entertainment Pack 2 attribution is WinWorld's.
